reason: The cited evidence shows carbon supports provide defective edge-plane nucleation sites for nanoparticle formation (E3) and that synthesis involves melting/fission on carbon (E1, E2), but none directly demonstrates that substrate defects lower the melting barrier or cause earlier premelting relative to free-standing nanoparticles. The key mechanistic premise of heterogeneous nucleation governing melting onset is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Carbon support defects act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for melting
Defective substrate reduces kinetic barrier to melting
Supported nanoparticles premelt at lower temperature than free-standing ones
Interfacial defects enhance atomic mobility at contact regions
